name: Propositional logic workspace
summary: Build bounded structured formulas, enumerate valuations, compare equivalence and inspect argument counterexamples.
assumptions: Explicit variable order; false before true and the final variable changes fastest. Classical NOT/AND/OR/implication/biconditional. Structured input only; no arbitrary text parsing or theorem proving.

name: Finite first-order structure workspace
summary: Evaluate structured sentences in a fully declared finite interpretation and inspect witnesses or counterexamples.
assumptions: Finite nonempty domain, named constants and explicitly interpreted predicates/relations. No invented Tarski geometry, arbitrary FOL theorem proving or automatic grading of open translations/constructions.

name: Proof planning workspace
summary: Organize assumptions, goals and justified steps, then reveal a rubric and reference reasoning.
assumptions: Open proof self-check only. Fields and reference reveal do not establish correctness, receive a numeric score or persist as verified evidence.

name: Recursion and induction workspace
summary: Evaluate a bounded recurrence and organize induction or invariant obligations.
assumptions: Numeric sequence evaluation is finite and deterministic. Induction, structural and invariant proofs are unscored self-checks; a finite trace is not a universal proof.

name: Tree and graph workspace
summary: Inspect ordered binary traversals and finite directed topological constraints.
assumptions: Explicit adjacency and left/right child structure determine meaning. Height counts edges: leaf 0, empty −1. Any proposed topological order must be checked against every edge; graph/tree construction is not compared to one drawing.

name: Finite sets workspace
summary: Inspect finite set operations, powersets and Cartesian products.
assumptions: Finite explicit objects only, with set and ordered-pair structure kept distinct. Complement needs an explicit universe. Open set proofs remain unscored.

name: Finite functions and relations workspace
summary: Check finite mapping well-definedness and injection/surjection, plus relation properties.
assumptions: Finite declared domain/codomain and explicit ordered pairs. Function validity is checked before properties. These finite checks do not prove arbitrary infinite-domain statements.
